text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike in cross-region spillover this morning from eu-west into us-west. Latency for tiered customers jumped and cost went up ~18% for the window. Any quick wins? :thinking:
kevin: Do we have per-region spill budgets configured? Last I checked we only had a global cap which is too coarse for hot regions.
olivia: We have per-customer budgets, not per-region. The routing layer treats region as a soft hint atm.
raj: Network flaps in eu-west-2 caused a drop in local capacity; autoscaler filled but it was slow. Requests started routing out after admission queue hit 90%.
maria: Proposed quick mitigation: enforce priority pools + a small spillover budget per region, and force fallback to lighter quantized model when spilling. Keeps tail latency down and cost predictable.
kevin: Agree. Quick config prototype (pushed to staging earlier):
```yaml
admission_control:
  pools:
    - name: premium
      weight: 0.6
      max_inflight: 1000
    - name: standard
      weight: 0.3
      max_inflight: 500
    - name: best_effort
      weight: 0.1
      max_inflight: 200
spillover:
  per_region_budget: 0.05 # fraction of region capacity
  fallback_model: "redwood-gpt-small-q4"
```
kevin: With that, spillover only triggers when region is near capacity and fallback happens automatically.
olivia: Two questions: 1) do we want to count fallback tokens against customer quota? 2) telemetry — we need clear tags so billing + SLO dashboards show when fallback happened.
raj: For (1) I vote yes — it's still charged but at lower rate. For (2) add tags `routing.spillover=true` and `model.fallback=<model>` to traces.
sre-bot: ALERT: eu-west-2 nodegroup instability detected 2026-03-18T07:49:12Z — increased error 429s on shard-4.
maria: ok that's the likely trigger. Can infra patch the nodegroup or we throttle proactively?
raj: I'll kick a rolling restart on shard-4 now, but we should assume 10-15m to stabilize. Meanwhile we need admission rules.
kevin: One more config snippet for admission thresholds (can be live updated):
```json
{
  "region_thresholds": {
    "eu-west-2": { "spill_at": 0.85, "reject_at": 0.95 },
    "us-west-1": { "spill_at": 0.9, "reject_at": 0.98 }
  },
  "tier_overrides": {
    "premium": {"spill_priority": 0},
    "standard": {"spill_priority": 1}
  }
}
```
olivia: That looks safe. We'll set eu-west-2 to be conservative for the next 24h. Also add a short TTL on queued requests: `queue_ttl_ms=1200` to avoid long tails.
maria: Agreed. Can someone create a quick runbook update for on-call so they know to flip the per-region budget and monitor `routing.spillover` metrics?
kevin: I'll create a small runbook entry and push to kb under infra/playbooks.
raj: Rolling restart done. Nodegroup reports healthy in cloud console.
sre-bot: INFO: shard-4 health restored at 2026-03-18T07:58:44Z. Error 429s back to baseline.
maria: Thanks — let's ship the admission rule change as a short-lived feature toggle (until we confirm no regressed QoE). deploy-bot: Deploy queued: admission-rule-20260318 -> staging -> 1912345699
kevin: Deploy done to staging. Running e2e smoke now.
olivia: If smoke looks good, promote to prod with the conservative eu-west-2 thresholds and enable telemetry tagging.
maria: Plan: (1) enable per-region spill budgets + fallback model toggle, (2) annotate telemetry, (3) update runbook. Check back in 30m. :thumbsup:
